messages.author: 536298a107e0f9e0
messages.subject: Rstan running time
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am currently working on the estimation of a hierarchical bayesian model. I noticed that usually it takes about 25 mins to run 100 iterations but however it takes FOREVER to run 500 iterations. Is the estimation time linear in terms of the number of iterations? In other words, should the running time for 500 iterations 5 times of the time for 100 iterations? The dataset contains only 1000 observations, and I believe the model per se is not complicated.

I noticed that sometimes for the 500 iterations, the viewer window would stop updating the progress (e.g., stop at 90% sampling). Is this caused by the memory limits or just my coding problem? 

Please let me know if you have any thoughts. The R script and data file are attached. 

Thanks in advance!

Best,
Austin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rstan running time
parts:
Run time is not linear in number of iterations because
the number of calls to log density and gradient calculations
(the real time sinks) changes. As adaptation runs
during warmup, it changes the parameters of the underlying Hamiltonian simulation.
If the step size and mass matrix produce small steps, it may seem like it'll never
finish. This is usually done in response to complex posterior geometry,
often arising in hierarchical models.

I have no idea about viewer windows in RStan, though.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rstan running time
parts:
For that model, we do not recommend the inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001)
priors, the normal(0, 100) priors or the inverse Wisharts.

You can also vectorize many of your other calls for more efficiency.

And you don't want to do things like create constant
diagonal matrices as local variables---they should be in
transformed data if you need them. But you really want to
use the cholesky factor parameterizations of covariance for
efficiency. See the manual chapter on regression for prior
recommendations and how to code them.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rstan running time
parts:
Unless you're somehow running out of memory (you can
check your system monitors depending on OS), a more
powerful computer's only going to be an incremental
improvement. You really need to code the model more
efficiently computationally or find a more efficient parameterization
statistically or work with less data.

Run time is very sensitive to data. If the model is
misspecified for the data, run time can be very long even
in cases where data generated from the model will fit easily.

We always recommend fake-data testing to start. Take a small
instance of your problem, generate fake data from the priors,
then see if you can fit it. If you find yourself saying "the priors
are too wide for simulation", then you probably want stronger
priors in your model.

- Bob
